name: EcoFlow Delta Pro
amazonQuery: EcoFlow Delta Pro portable power station
summary: EcoFlow's original 3.6kWh, 3,600W LiFePO4 power station: a silent, indoor-safe battery for fridges, CPAPs and home essentials, best for buyers who find it discounted against the newer Delta Pro 3.
verdict:
The Delta Pro is still a capable whole-room battery, but it is now the older 120V sibling of the Delta Pro 3, so buy it on price. EcoFlow rates it at 3,600Wh of [LiFePO4](/glossary/lifepo4/) storage and 3,600W of continuous output, with a 7,200W surge and an X-Boost mode that lets resistive loads up to 4,500W run at reduced power.

**Do the fridge math first.** About 85% of the rated [watt-hours](/glossary/watt-hours/) reaches your appliances after inverter losses, so call it roughly 3,000Wh usable. A modern fridge averaging 100W, plus a modem, a CPAP and some LED lights at about 150W combined, adds up to 250W. That gives you around 12 hours, or about a day and a half with the fridge alone. Check your own loads with the [power station runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/).

**Charging is the real strength.** The spec sheet lists 1,800W of AC charging on a 120V outlet, up to 3,000W from a 240V outlet, and 1,600W of solar input across an 11–150V range. With strong sun and a large array, it can refill in a single day. Two Smart Extra Batteries take it to 10.8kWh.

**The limits.** At 99 pounds it rolls on wheels instead of being carried, and one unit is 120V only. A 240V well pump needs the newer [EcoFlow Delta Pro 3](/gear/ecoflow-delta-pro-3/) or two linked units.

Owners praise the fast charging and the app. The main complaint is weight. It appears in the [best home generator for power outages](/best-home-generator-for-power-outages/) guide.

summary: Anker's 3,840Wh, 6,000W power station with 120/240V output and NEMA 14-50 and L14-30 outlets, built to run well pumps and home circuits and to grow to about 26.9kWh.
verdict:
The F3800 is the strongest single-box battery for 240V loads, which is why it leads for well pumps and RV hookups. Anker rates it at 3,840Wh of [LiFePO4](/glossary/lifepo4/) storage and 6,000W continuous at 120/240V.

**The 240V outlets are the point.** It has both an [L14-30](/glossary/l14-30/) and a NEMA 14-50, each rated up to 6,000W. The L14-30 feeds a home panel through a [transfer switch](/glossary/transfer-switch/) or Anker's home backup hardware, installed by an electrician. The 14-50 plugs straight into a 50A RV cord. With 6,000W continuous, it has real headroom for a 3/4 or 1 HP submersible pump start.

**Runtime math.** About 3,250Wh is usable. A typical household's daily well pumping uses well under 1kWh, so the pump barely dents it. A fridge, freezer, internet and lights at about 300W run for roughly 11 hours. Six BP3800 expansion batteries take one unit to about 26.9kWh for multi-day outages.

**Solar keeps it going.** Two 1,200W inputs accept 2,400W of solar in total, and AC charging runs at up to 1,800W. A good array can replace a full day of essentials use in strong sun.

Owners praise the output and the RV-ready outlets. The main complaint is the 132.3-pound weight. It features in the [best generator for well pump](/best-generator-for-well-pump/), [best home battery backup](/best-home-battery-backup/) and [best Anker power station](/best-anker-solix-power-station/) guides. verdict:
The Delta Pro 3 is the power station to buy if you need 240V from one box without stepping up to a home battery. EcoFlow rates it at 4,096Wh of [LiFePO4](/glossary/lifepo4/) storage and 4,000W continuous, with an 8,000W surge, at either 120V or 240V.

Owners report quiet operation and a polished app. The main complaint is the weight on stairs. It features in the [best generator for well pump](/best-generator-for-well-pump/) and [best portable power station for home backup](/best-portable-power-station-for-home-backup/) guides.

name: Goal Zero Yeti 1500X
amazonQuery: Goal Zero Yeti 1500X portable power station
summary: Goal Zero's 1,516Wh, 2,000W NMC lithium power station with a 600W solar port and Yeti expansion and home-integration accessories, a rugged choice for cabins and overlanding rigs.
verdict:
The Yeti 1500X is a tough, proven station for cabins and overland rigs, but its older battery chemistry makes LiFePO4 rivals the better buy for daily cycling. Goal Zero rates it at 1,516Wh with 2,000W continuous and a 3,500W surge.

**The chemistry trade-off.** The battery is lithium [NMC](/glossary/nmc-battery/), not [LiFePO4](/glossary/lifepo4/). It was rated for about 500 cycles to 80% at launch, against 3,000 or more for most LFP units. For a cabin kit or an emergency box that sees occasional deep cycles, that is fine. For a station you drain and refill every day, an LFP unit will last years longer.

**Size it to your loads.** About 1,290Wh is usable. A fridge averaging 100W runs for roughly 13 hours. The 3,500W surge starts a refrigerator or a small power tool with room to spare. Check your loads with the [power station runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/).

**Charging is slow out of the box.** The standard wall charger is 120W, so a full refill takes many hours. Goal Zero sells a 600W power supply separately. The high-power solar port takes up to 600W at 14–50V, which suits a cabin array. Yeti expansion systems add capacity for longer outages.

**Know the limits.** It has only two 120V AC outlets, weighs about 45.6 pounds, and some retailers now list it as discontinued.

Owners praise the build and the accessory range. The main complaint is the cost per watt-hour. It appears in the [best portable power station](/best-portable-power-station/) roundup. For LFP at a similar size, see the [Jackery Explorer 1000 Plus](/gear/jackery-explorer-1000-plus/).

verdict:
